questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Bamako?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Mali is Bamako.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Mali about 1,240,192 square kilometres; Nigeria about 923,768 square kilometres; Burkina Faso about 274,200 square kilometres; Togo about 56,785 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Mali?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mali article.

questions.proof: Mali's capital and most populated city is Bamako.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Mali?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Mali on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mali article.

questions.proof: Mali is bordered by Algeria on the North, Niger on the east, Burkina Faso and the Côte d'Ivoire on the south, Guinea on the south-west, and Senegal and Mauritania on the west.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Mali on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Mali on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
